at udarbejde.explanation: "At udarbejde" means "to prepare", as in drawing up a document such as a report or a contract. It is built from "ud" (out) and "at arbejde" (to work). For everyday things like food, use "at lave" (to make): "Jeg laver mad" (I am making food).

sentence.da: Vi skal **udarbejde** en plan, før projektet kan starte.
sentence.en: We must draw up a plan before the project can start.

at udbetale.explanation: "At udbetale" means "to pay out". To say a salary is paid: "Lønnen bliver udbetalt den første" (The salary is paid out on the first). The opposite is "at indbetale" (to pay in). For example, "Jeg indbetaler penge på kontoen" (I pay money into the account).

sentence.da: Kommunen skal **udbetale** pengene den første i måneden.
sentence.en: The municipality must pay out the money on the first of the month.

at udbrede.explanation: "At udbrede" means "to spread", as in making an idea or news reach more people. For butter, use "at smøre" (to spread): "Jeg smører brødet" (I spread butter on the bread).

sentence.da: Avisen vil **udbrede** nyheden til hele landet.
sentence.en: The newspaper wants to spread the news to the whole country.

at udbygge.explanation: "At udbygge" means "to expand". It is built from "ud" (out) and "at bygge" (to build). To say a city adds to its roads: "De udbygger vejnettet" (They are expanding the road network).

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **udbygge** cykelstierne i hele byen.
sentence.en: The municipality wants to expand the bike paths across the whole city.

at uddanne.explanation: "At uddanne" means "to educate", as in training someone for a profession. To say who does the training: "Hospitalet uddanner sygeplejersker" (The hospital trains nurses). To say you train yourself, add "sig" (yourself): "Jeg uddanner mig til lærer" (I am training to be a teacher).

sentence.da: Det tager tre år at **uddanne** en tømrer.
sentence.en: It takes three years to train a carpenter.

at uddele.explanation: "At uddele" means "to hand out". To say someone gives things to a group: "Læreren uddeler opgaver" (The teacher hands out assignments). To say a prize is awarded, use "at tildele" (to award): "Hun blev tildelt prisen" (She was awarded the prize).

sentence.da: Frivillige vil **uddele** gratis mad til de hjemløse.
sentence.en: Volunteers will hand out free food to the homeless.

at udelade.explanation: "At udelade" means "to leave out". It is built from "ud" (out) and "at lade" (to let). To say you skip an ingredient: "Jeg udelader sukker i kaffen" (I leave sugar out of my coffee).

sentence.da: Du kan **udelade** sukkeret, hvis kagen er sød nok.
sentence.en: You can leave out the sugar if the cake is sweet enough.

at udfase.explanation: "At udfase" means "to phase out". It is built from "ud" (out) and "en fase" (a phase). The opposite is "at indfase" (to phase in). For example, "Kommunen indfaser en ny ordning" (The municipality is phasing in a new scheme).

sentence.da: Regeringen vil **udfase** kul inden for ti år.
sentence.en: The government will phase out coal within ten years.

at udfordre.explanation: "At udfordre" means "to challenge". To challenge someone to a contest, add "til" (to): "Jeg udfordrer dig til et løb" (I challenge you to a race).

sentence.da: Svære opgaver kan **udfordre** dig, så du bliver dygtigere.
sentence.en: Hard tasks can challenge you so you become more skilled.

at udforme.explanation: "At udforme" means "to design". It is built from "ud" (out) and "en form" (a shape). To say you design a plan: "Vi udformer en plan" (We are designing a plan).

sentence.da: Juristerne skal **udforme** et forslag til en ny lov.
sentence.en: The lawyers must draft a proposal for a new law.

at udforske.explanation: "At udforske" means "to explore". It is built from "ud" (out) and "at forske" (to research). To say you explore a city: "Vi udforsker byen til fods" (We explore the city on foot).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **udforske** den gamle bydel i morgen.
sentence.en: I want to explore the old part of town tomorrow.

at udfylde.explanation: "At udfylde" means "to fill in". To say you complete a form: "Hun udfylder ansøgningen" (She fills in the application). To fill a glass, use "at fylde" (to fill): "Jeg fylder glasset" (I fill the glass).

forms.en: I have filled in / filled out

sentence.da: Du skal **udfylde** hele formularen og skrive under.
sentence.en: You have to fill out the whole form and sign it.

at udføre.explanation: "At udføre" means "to carry out". To say someone does a job: "Han udfører arbejdet" (He carries out the work). To say you run a test: "Vi udfører en test" (We are running a test).

sentence.da: Hun skal **udføre** opgaven før fredag.
sentence.en: She has to carry out the task before Friday.

at udgive.explanation: "At udgive" means "to publish". To say someone pretends to be someone else, add "sig for" (oneself as): "Han udgav sig for en læge" (He posed as a doctor).

sentence.da: Forfatteren vil **udgive** sin nye roman i foråret.
sentence.en: The author wants to publish his new novel in the spring.

at udgrave.explanation: "At udgrave" means "to excavate". It is built from "ud" (out) and "at grave" (to dig). To say a team digs up old remains: "De udgraver en gammel gravplads" (They are excavating an old burial site).

sentence.da: Arkæologerne vil **udgrave** en gammel boplads ved fjorden.
sentence.en: The archaeologists will excavate an old settlement by the fjord.

at udgå.explanation: "At udgå" means "to be dropped". To say a product is taken out of a range: "Mælken udgår af sortimentet" (The milk is dropped from the range). To name the source something originates from, add "fra" (from): "Forslaget udgår fra ministeriet" (The proposal originates with the ministry).

sentence.da: Varen vil **udgå**, så butikken sælger den billigt.
sentence.en: The item will be discontinued, so the store sells it cheaply.

at udgøre.explanation: "At udgøre" means "to constitute". To say what share something makes up: "Kvinder udgør halvdelen af klassen" (Women make up half of the class). To say something is dangerous, use it with "fare" (danger): "Det udgør en fare" (It poses a danger).

sentence.da: Børn kan **udgøre** en tredjedel af gæsterne.
sentence.en: Children can make up a third of the guests.

at udløbe.explanation: "At udløbe" means "to expire". It is built from "ud" (out) and "at løbe" (to run), so a time limit runs out. To ask when a document stops being valid: "Hvornår udløber dit pas?" (When does your passport expire?)

sentence.da: Tilbuddet kan **udløbe** om en uge, så du skal skynde dig.
sentence.en: The offer can expire in a week, so you must hurry.

at udløse.explanation: "At udløse" means "to trigger". To say something sets off an alarm: "Røgen udløste alarmen" (The smoke set off the alarm). Do not mix it up with "at udløbe" (to expire). For example, "Mit pas udløber i maj" (My passport expires in May).

sentence.da: Støvet kan **udløse** allergi hos nogle børn.
sentence.en: The dust can trigger allergies in some children.

at udmærke sig.explanation: "At udmærke sig" means "to excel". To name the quality you stand out for, add "ved" (for): "Hun udmærker sig ved sin flid" (She stands out for her hard work).

sentence.da: Hun vil **udmærke sig** i musik, fordi hun øver hver dag.
sentence.en: She will excel in music because she practices every day.

at udnytte.explanation: "At udnytte" means "to make use of". To say you make the most of your time: "at udnytte tiden" (to make the most of the time). About a person, it turns negative. For example, "Han udnytter sine kolleger" (He takes advantage of his colleagues).

forms.en: I have exploited / made use of

sentence.da: Vi bør **udnytte** det gode vejr og tage på stranden.
sentence.en: We should make the most of the nice weather and go to the beach.

at udnævne.explanation: "At udnævne" means "to appoint". To name the position, add "til" (as): "udnævne nogen til dommer" (appoint someone as a judge).

sentence.da: Statsministeren vil **udnævne** en ny minister i dag.
sentence.en: The prime minister will appoint a new minister today.

at udrette.explanation: "At udrette" means "to accomplish". To say you cannot get anything done: "Jeg kan ikke udrette noget" (I cannot accomplish anything). To ask what can be done about a problem: "Hvad kan vi udrette?" (What can we do about it?)

sentence.da: Vi kan ikke **udrette** meget uden hjælp fra naboerne.
sentence.en: We cannot accomplish much without help from the neighbors.

at udrydde.explanation: "At udrydde" means "to eradicate". It is built from "ud" (out) and "at rydde" (to clear).

sentence.da: Lægerne håber at kunne **udrydde** sygdommen helt.
sentence.en: The doctors hope to be able to eradicate the disease completely.

at udsende.explanation: "At udsende" means "to broadcast". It is built from "ud" (out) and "at sende" (to send). To say something gives off light: "Solen udsender lys og varme" (The sun gives off light and heat).

sentence.da: Radiostationen vil **udsende** nyheder hver time.
sentence.en: The radio station will broadcast news every hour.

at udskifte.explanation: "At udskifte" means "to replace". To say you put a new part in place of an old one: "Jeg udskifter pæren" (I am replacing the light bulb).

sentence.da: Du skal **udskifte** batteriet, når det er tomt.
sentence.en: You must replace the battery when it is empty.

at udslette.explanation: "At udslette" means "to wipe out". It is built from "ud" (out) and "at slette" (to erase).

sentence.da: Stormen kunne **udslette** hele landsbyen på få timer.
sentence.en: The storm could wipe out the whole village in a few hours.

at udstede.explanation: "At udstede" means "to issue". To say a bank gives out a card: "Banken udsteder et kort" (The bank issues a card). For a book or a magazine, use "at udgive" (to publish): "Forlaget udgiver bogen" (The publisher publishes the book).

sentence.da: Politiet kan **udstede** en bøde, hvis du kører for stærkt.
sentence.en: The police can issue a fine if you drive too fast.

at udstille.explanation: "At udstille" means "to exhibit". To say art is put on display: "Galleriet udstiller billeder" (The gallery exhibits pictures). To say someone is shown up in public, use it for a person: "Aviserne udstillede ham som løgner" (The papers exposed him as a liar).

sentence.da: Museet vil **udstille** malerier fra 1800-tallet i sommer.
sentence.en: The museum will exhibit paintings from the 1800s this summer.

at udsætte.explanation: "At udsætte" means "to postpone". To say a decision is put off: "Beslutningen er udsat til næste uge" (The decision is postponed until next week). To say you expose yourself to something unpleasant, add "sig for" (yourself to): "at udsætte sig for fare" (to expose yourself to danger).

sentence.da: Vi må **udsætte** mødet, fordi mange er syge.
sentence.en: We must postpone the meeting because many people are sick.

at udtale.explanation: "At udtale" means "to pronounce". The noun is "en udtale" (a pronunciation). To compliment someone's speech: "Din udtale er god" (Your pronunciation is good).

sentence.da: Kan du **udtale** dit navn for mig?
sentence.en: Can you pronounce your name for me?

at udtrykke.explanation: "At udtrykke" means "to express". To say someone voices an opinion: "Han udtrykker sin mening" (He expresses his opinion). To say how someone speaks, add "sig" (oneself): "Hun udtrykker sig klart" (She expresses herself clearly).

sentence.da: Det er svært at **udtrykke** sine følelser på et fremmedsprog.
sentence.en: It is hard to express your feelings in a foreign language.

at udveksle.explanation: "At udveksle" means "to exchange". To say people give each other greetings: "De udvekslede hilsner" (They exchanged greetings). To swap an item for another, use "at bytte" (to swap): "Jeg bytter trøjen" (I am swapping the sweater).

sentence.da: Vi kan **udveksle** telefonnumre, så vi kan holde kontakt.
sentence.en: We can exchange phone numbers so we can keep in touch.

at udvide.explanation: "At udvide" means "to expand". To say a company grows its premises: "Firmaet udvider med et nyt kontor" (The company is expanding with a new office). For something that grows by itself, use "at vokse" (to grow): "Byen vokser" (The town grows).

sentence.da: De vil **udvide** huset, fordi familien bliver større.
sentence.en: They want to expand the house because the family is getting bigger.

at udvikle.explanation: "At udvikle" means "to develop". To say someone grows and changes, add "sig" (oneself): "Børn udvikler sig hurtigt" (Children develop quickly).

sentence.da: De vil **udvikle** en ny app til børn.
sentence.en: They want to develop a new app for children.

at udvikle sig.explanation: "At udvikle sig" means "to develop". To say someone improves step by step: "Hun udvikler sig som musiker" (She is developing as a musician). The "sig" (oneself) is needed for this meaning. To say someone builds something, use "at udvikle" without "sig": "at udvikle en app" (to develop an app).

sentence.da: Børn kan **udvikle sig** meget, når de leger med andre.
sentence.en: Children can develop a lot when they play with others.

at udvælge.explanation: "At udvælge" means "to select". To say you pick a few from many: "Hun udvælger de bedste billeder" (She selects the best photos). For a quick choice, use "at vælge" (to choose): "Jeg vælger kaffe" (I choose coffee).

sentence.da: Læreren skal **udvælge** fem elever til konkurrencen.
sentence.en: The teacher must select five students for the competition.

at underholde.explanation: "At underholde" means "to entertain". With "sig" (oneself), it means to chat. For example, "De underholdt sig hele aftenen" (They chatted all evening).

sentence.da: Klovnen skal **underholde** børnene til festen.
sentence.en: The clown must entertain the children at the party.

at underkaste sig.explanation: "At underkaste sig" means "to submit to". To say people accept a rule, name it after the verb: "De måtte underkaste sig reglerne" (They had to submit to the rules). It is built from "under" (under) and "at kaste" (to throw).

sentence.da: Han ville ikke **underkaste sig** kongens vilje.
sentence.en: He would not submit to the king's will.

at underminere.explanation: "At underminere" means "to undermine". To say someone weakens authority: "Han underminerer lærerens autoritet" (He undermines the teacher's authority).

sentence.da: Løgne kan **underminere** tilliden mellem kollegaer.
sentence.en: Lies can undermine the trust between colleagues.

at underrette.explanation: "At underrette" means "to notify". To say you tell the police about an accident: "Jeg underretter politiet om uheldet" (I notify the police about the accident).

sentence.da: Skolen skal **underrette** forældrene om ændringen i tide.
sentence.en: The school must notify the parents about the change in time.

at underskrive.explanation: "At underskrive" means "to sign". It is built from "under" (under) and "at skrive" (to write), because you write your name under the text. To say you sign an agreement, use it with the agreement: "Jeg underskriver aftalen" (I sign the agreement). The same meaning can be said with "at skrive under" (to sign). For example, "Skriv under her" (Sign here).

sentence.da: Du skal **underskrive** papiret her.
sentence.en: You have to sign the paper here.

at understrege.explanation: "At understrege" means "to emphasize". It is built from "under" (under) and "streg" (a line), so you put a line under a point. When you draw a line under written words, it means "to underline": "Understreg ordet" (Underline the word).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **understrege**, at dette er meget vigtigt.
sentence.en: I would like to emphasize that this is very important.

at understøtte.explanation: "At understøtte" means "to support". When you back an idea with facts, use it with the idea: "Tallene understøtter hans teori" (The numbers support his theory). When a program or device can work with something, use it for that: "Programmet understøtter flere sprog" (The program supports several languages).

sentence.da: Kommunen vil **understøtte** foreningen med penge hvert år.
sentence.en: The municipality wants to support the association with money every year.

at undersøge.explanation: "At undersøge" means "to examine or investigate". It is built from "under" (under) and "at søge" (to search). To say a doctor checks a patient, use it with the patient: "Lægen undersøger mig" (The doctor examines me).

sentence.da: Politiet vil **undersøge** sagen.
sentence.en: The police want to investigate the case.

at undertrykke.explanation: "At undertrykke" means "to suppress or oppress". When you hold in a feeling or a sound, use it with that feeling: "undertrykke et gab" (suppress a yawn). When a group of people is kept down by force or unfair rules, use it with the group: "Regimet undertrykker mindretallet" (The regime oppresses the minority).

sentence.da: Diktatoren ville **undertrykke** folket med frygt og vold.
sentence.en: The dictator wanted to oppress the people with fear and violence.

at undervise.explanation: "At undervise" means "to teach". To say which subject you teach, add "i" (in) before it: "Hun underviser i matematik" (She teaches math). The person who learns uses a different verb, "at lære" (to learn). For example, "Jeg lærer dansk" (I am learning Danish).

sentence.da: Min søster skal **undervise** en klasse i morgen.
sentence.en: My sister is going to teach a class tomorrow.

at undervurdere.explanation: "At undervurdere" means "to underestimate". It is built from "under" (under) and "at vurdere" (to assess), so you rate something too low. To warn someone, say: "Undervurder ikke opgaven" (Do not underestimate the task).

sentence.da: Man skal ikke **undervurdere** en modstander, der træner hver dag.
sentence.en: You must not underestimate an opponent who trains every day.

at undgå.explanation: "At undgå" means "to avoid". To say you stay away from a food, use it with that food: "Jeg undgår sukker" (I avoid sugar). To say you stop something from happening, use "at forhindre" (to prevent) instead: "Vi forhindrer ulykken" (We prevent the accident).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **undgå** trafikken om morgenen.
sentence.en: I would like to avoid the traffic in the morning.

at undlade.explanation: "At undlade" means "to omit". To say you leave a word or a detail out of a text, use "at udelade" (to leave out) instead: "Jeg udelader navnet" (I leave out the name).

sentence.da: Du bør **undlade** at stille personlige spørgsmål til fremmede.
sentence.en: You should refrain from asking strangers personal questions.

at undre sig.explanation: "At undre sig" means "to wonder". To name the thing that surprises you, add "over" (about): "Jeg undrer mig over prisen" (I am surprised at the price). To ask yourself a question, use "Jeg gad vide" (I wonder): "Jeg gad vide, hvad klokken er" (I wonder what time it is).

sentence.da: Man kan **undre sig** over, hvorfor bussen aldrig kommer til tiden.
sentence.en: You can wonder why the bus never comes on time.

at undskylde.explanation: "At undskylde" means "to apologize". The short word "Undskyld" means "Sorry" when you made a mistake. For example, "Undskyld, jeg kom for sent" (Sorry, I was late). It means "Excuse me" when you want someone's attention. For another example, "Undskyld, hvor er toilettet?" (Excuse me, where is the toilet?). To name the mistake you apologize for, add "for" (for): "Jeg undskylder for forsinkelsen" (I apologize for the delay).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **undskylde** for det.
sentence.en: I would like to apologize for that.

at undslippe.explanation: "At undslippe" means "to escape". To say what you escape from, put the thing right after it, with no word for "from": "undslippe faren" (escape the danger).

sentence.da: Ræven kan **undslippe** jægeren ved at løbe ind i skoven.
sentence.en: The fox can escape the hunter by running into the forest.

at undvære.explanation: "At undvære" means "to do without". To say you need something every day, use it with "ikke" (not): "Jeg kan ikke undvære min telefon" (I cannot do without my phone). To ask if someone can spare something for a while, use it in a question: "Kan du undvære bilen i dag?" (Can you spare the car today?)

sentence.da: Mange kan ikke **undvære** kaffen om morgenen.
sentence.en: Many people cannot do without coffee in the morning.

at uploade.explanation: "At uploade" means "to upload". It is borrowed from the English word "upload". To tell someone to upload something, use the short command form: "Upload dokumentet her" (Upload the document here).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **uploade** billederne til hjemmesiden.
sentence.en: I want to upload the photos to the website.

en ubalance.explanation: "En ubalance" means "an imbalance". The start "u-" turns a word into its opposite, as in "uvenlig" (unfriendly). To say where things are out of balance, add "i" (in): "en ubalance i økonomien" (an imbalance in the economy).

sentence.da: Der er en **ubalance** mellem arbejde og fritid i mit liv.
sentence.en: There is an imbalance between work and free time in my life.

en ubåd.explanation: "En ubåd" means "a submarine". It is short for "en undervandsbåd" (literally, an underwater boat).

sentence.da: En **ubåd** kan sejle under vandet i flere uger.
sentence.en: A submarine can sail under the water for several weeks.

en udbetaling.explanation: "En udbetaling" means "a payout". It is built from "ud" (out) and "en betaling" (a payment). When you buy a home, it also means the down payment: "en udbetaling på 200.000 kroner" (a down payment of 200,000 kroner).

sentence.da: Hver måned får han en **udbetaling** fra sin pension.
sentence.en: Every month he gets a payout from his pension.

en uddannelse.explanation: "En uddannelse" means "an education". To say you are training for a job, use it with "at tage" (to take): "Hun tager en uddannelse som sygeplejerske" (She is training to be a nurse).

sentence.da: Han har en god **uddannelse** og et godt job.
sentence.en: He has a good education and a good job.

en udenrigsminister.explanation: "En udenrigsminister" means "a foreign minister". The start "udenrigs-" means "foreign", as in "udenrigspolitik" (foreign policy).

sentence.da: Danmarks **udenrigsminister** mødte en kollega fra Tyskland i går.
sentence.en: Denmark's foreign minister met a colleague from Germany yesterday.

en udenrigsrejse.explanation: "En udenrigsrejse" means "a trip abroad". It is built from "udenrigs" (foreign) and "en rejse" (a journey). The start "udenrigs-" is also in "udenrigsminister" (foreign minister).

sentence.da: Min første **udenrigsrejse** gik til Tyskland.
sentence.en: My first trip abroad went to Germany.

en udflugt.explanation: "En udflugt" means "an excursion". It is built from "ud" (out) and "flugt" (escape). To say where the group is right now, use "på" (on): "Børnene er på udflugt" (The children are on an excursion).

sentence.da: I morgen tager vi på **udflugt** til stranden.
sentence.en: Tomorrow we are going on an excursion to the beach.

en udfordring.explanation: "En udfordring" means "a challenge". It comes from "at udfordre" (to challenge). To say you face one, use "at stå over for" (to face): "Vi står over for en ny udfordring" (We face a new challenge).

sentence.da: At lære dansk er en stor **udfordring**.
sentence.en: Learning Danish is a big challenge.

en udgang.explanation: "En udgang" means "an exit". On a highway, use "en afkørsel" (an exit ramp) instead: "Tag næste afkørsel" (Take the next exit).

sentence.da: Der er en **udgang** bag ved butikken.
sentence.en: There is an exit behind the store.

en udgave.explanation: "En udgave" means "an edition", as in a printing of a book. It also means "a version" of something, such as a film. For example, "Jeg har set den nye udgave af filmen" (I have seen the new version of the film).

sentence.da: Den nye **udgave** af bogen har flere billeder end den gamle.
sentence.en: The new edition of the book has more pictures than the old one.

en udgift.explanation: "En udgift" means "an expense". Its opposite is "en indtægt" (an income). For example, "Vi har flere udgifter end indtægter" (We have more expenses than income). To talk about costs that stay the same every month, use "faste udgifter" (fixed expenses).

sentence.da: Husleje er min største **udgift** hver måned.
sentence.en: Rent is my biggest expense every month.

en udgivelse.explanation: "En udgivelse" means "a release". Do not mix it up with "en udgave" (an edition). To talk about the date something comes out, use "udgivelse": "Udgivelsen af albummet blev udsat" (The release of the album was postponed). To say which version of a book you have, use "udgave": "Jeg har den danske udgave" (I have the Danish edition).

sentence.da: Bandets nye **udgivelse** kommer på hylderne i næste uge.
sentence.en: The band's new release hits the shelves next week.

en udklædning.explanation: "En udklædning" means "a costume". It comes from "at klæde sig ud" (to dress up). To say you dress up as something, use "som" (as): "Jeg klæder mig ud som pirat" (I dress up as a pirate). In Denmark, children wear a costume at "fastelavn" (a holiday in February or March).

sentence.da: Børnene har **udklædning** på og ligner prinsesser og pirater.
sentence.en: The children are dressed up and look like princesses and pirates.

en udlejer.explanation: "En udlejer" means "a landlord". It comes from the verb "at udleje" (to rent out). To say you rent out your home, use the verb: "Jeg udlejer min lejlighed" (I rent out my apartment).

sentence.da: Jeg betaler huslejen til min **udlejer** hver måned.
sentence.en: I pay the rent to my landlord every month.

en udlejningsbil.explanation: "En udlejningsbil" means "a rental car". It is built from "udlejning" (renting out) and "bil" (car). The word "udlejning" is in other words too, as in "cykeludlejning" (bike rental).

sentence.da: Vi henter vores **udlejningsbil** i lufthavnen.
sentence.en: We pick up our rental car at the airport.

en udlånstid.explanation: "En udlånstid" means "a loan period". It is built from "udlån" (lending out) and "tid" (time). To ask how long you may keep a book, say: "Hvad er udlånstiden?" (What is the loan period?)

sentence.da: Bibliotekets **udlånstid** er fire uger, og så skal bogen tilbage.
sentence.en: The library's loan period is four weeks, and then the book must go back.

en udlænding.explanation: "En udlænding" means "a foreigner". It is built from "ud" (out) and "et land" (a country), like "udlandet" (abroad).

sentence.da: Han er **udlænding** og kommer fra Brasilien.
sentence.en: He is a foreigner and comes from Brazil.

en udnævnelse.explanation: "En udnævnelse" means "an appointment", as in being named to a job or title. To talk about a meeting with a doctor, use "en aftale" (an appointment) instead: "Jeg har en aftale hos lægen i morgen" (I have an appointment at the doctor tomorrow).

sentence.da: Hendes **udnævnelse** til direktør glædede hele afdelingen.
sentence.en: Her appointment as director pleased the whole department.

en udryddelse.explanation: "En udryddelse" means "an extinction". To say pests are wiped out on purpose, add "af" (of) and the pests: "en udryddelse af rotter" (an extermination of rats).

sentence.da: Dyret er truet af **udryddelse**, fordi skoven bliver fældet.
sentence.en: The animal is threatened with extinction because the forest is being cut down.

en udsendelse.explanation: "En udsendelse" means "a broadcast". When a soldier or aid worker is sent to work abroad, it means "deployment": "Hans udsendelse varer seks måneder" (His deployment lasts six months).

sentence.da: Vi ser en **udsendelse** om dyr på tv hver torsdag.
sentence.en: We watch a show about animals on TV every Thursday.

en udsigt.explanation: "En udsigt" means "a view". When you talk about what is expected to happen, it means "prospect" and is used with "til" (of): "Der er udsigt til regn" (Rain is expected).

sentence.da: Vi har en flot **udsigt** over havet.
sentence.en: We have a beautiful view of the sea.

en udskiftning.explanation: "En udskiftning" means "a replacement", as in swapping an old part for a new one. It is built from "ud" (out) and "at skifte" (to change). To say you swap something out, use "at skifte ud" (to swap out): "Vi skifter dækkene ud" (We swap the tires out).

sentence.da: En **udskiftning** af vinduerne koster mange penge.
sentence.en: Replacing the windows costs a lot of money.

en udskrivning.explanation: "En udskrivning" means "a discharge (from hospital)". It comes from the verb "at udskrive" (to discharge). To say a patient is allowed to go home, use the verb: "Han bliver udskrevet i morgen" (He is being discharged tomorrow).

sentence.da: Efter **udskrivning** fra hospitalet skal du hvile derhjemme.
sentence.en: After discharge from the hospital, you must rest at home.

en udstilling.explanation: "En udstilling" means "an exhibition". It comes from the verb "at udstille" (to exhibit). To say a museum shows something, use the verb: "Museet udstiller hans billeder" (The museum exhibits his paintings).

sentence.da: Kunstneren viser sine billeder i en **udstilling**.
sentence.en: The artist shows her pictures in an exhibition.

en udstrækning.explanation: "En udstrækning" means "a stretch", as in loosening your muscles. When you talk about how far something goes, it means "extent": "i stor udstrækning" (to a large extent).

sentence.da: Jeg laver **udstrækning** efter træning, og benene bliver mindre ømme.
sentence.en: I do stretching after training, and my legs get less sore.

en udstødning.explanation: "En udstødning" means "an exhaust", as on a car. When a person is pushed out of a group, it means "exclusion": "social udstødning" (social exclusion).

sentence.da: Der kommer sort røg ud af bilens **udstødning**.
sentence.en: Black smoke comes out of the car's exhaust.

en udtale.explanation: "En udtale" means "a pronunciation". It comes from the verb "at udtale" (to pronounce). To ask how to say a word, use the verb: "Hvordan udtaler man ordet?" (How do you pronounce the word?)

sentence.da: Din **udtale** er god, og jeg forstår dig.
sentence.en: Your pronunciation is good and I understand you.

en udtalelse.explanation: "En udtalelse" means "a statement". To say someone gave an official statement, say: "Direktøren afgav en udtalelse til pressen" (The director gave a statement to the press). Do not mix it up with "en udtale" (a pronunciation). To talk about how a word sounds, say: "Hendes udtale er god" (Her pronunciation is good).

sentence.da: Ministeren gav en kort **udtalelse** efter mødet.
sentence.en: The minister gave a short statement after the meeting.

en udvej.explanation: "En udvej" means "a way out". It is built from "ud" (out) and "en vej" (a road). To say you search for a solution, use it with "at finde" (to find): "at finde en udvej" (to find a way out).

sentence.da: Vi har ingen penge, og vi kan ikke se nogen **udvej**.
sentence.en: We have no money, and we cannot see any way out.

en udveksling.explanation: "En udveksling" means "an exchange". To talk about a school or university stay abroad, it is part of "en udvekslingsstudent" (an exchange student).

sentence.da: Min datter tager på **udveksling** til USA i et år.
sentence.en: My daughter is going to the USA on exchange for a year.

en udvidelse.explanation: "En udvidelse" means "an expansion". To say a company grows, use the verb "at udvide" (to expand): "Firmaet vil udvide" (The company wants to expand).

sentence.da: Vi bygger en **udvidelse** af huset, fordi børnene har brug for mere plads.
sentence.en: We are building an expansion of the house because the children need more space.

en udvikler.explanation: "En udvikler" means "a developer". It comes from the verb "at udvikle" (to develop). To say what kind of developer, put a word in front: "en softwareudvikler" (a software developer).

sentence.da: Min bror er **udvikler** og laver apps til telefoner.
sentence.en: My brother is a developer and makes apps for phones.

en udvikling.explanation: "En udvikling" means "a development". It comes from the verb "at udvikle" (to develop). To say a place changes over time, use the verb with "sig" (itself): "Byen udvikler sig hurtigt" (The city is developing fast).

sentence.da: Et barns **udvikling** tager mange år.
sentence.en: A child's development takes many years.

en uenighed.explanation: "En uenighed" means "a disagreement". The start "u-" turns a word into its opposite, as in "en enighed" (an agreement). To say that you personally disagree, use the adjective "uenig": "Jeg er uenig" (I disagree).

sentence.da: Vi havde en **uenighed** om, hvem der skulle betale.
sentence.en: We had a disagreement about who should pay.

en uge.explanation: "En uge" means "a week". To say "next week", say: "Jeg rejser i næste uge" (I am traveling next week). To say "this week", say: "Jeg har travlt i denne uge" (I am busy this week). To name a week by its number, say: "uge 42" (week 42).

sentence.da: En **uge** har syv dage.
sentence.en: A week has seven days.

en ugeavis.explanation: "En ugeavis" means "a weekly local paper". It is built from "en uge" (a week) and "en avis" (a newspaper). To say where you read something, add "i" (in): "Det stod i ugeavisen" (It was in the weekly paper).

sentence.da: Vi får en **ugeavis** i postkassen hver uge.
sentence.en: We get a weekly local paper in the mailbox every week.

en ugedag.explanation: "En ugedag" means "a day of the week". It is built from "uge" (week) and "dag" (day). Inside a sentence, a day name is written without a capital, unlike in English. For example, "mandag" (Monday).

sentence.da: Mandag er en **ugedag**.
sentence.en: Monday is a day of the week.

en ugeplan.explanation: "En ugeplan" means "a weekly plan". It is built from "en uge" (a week) and "en plan" (a plan). To ask what is on it, say: "Hvad står der på ugeplanen?" (What does the weekly plan say?)

sentence.da: Børnene får en **ugeplan** fra skolen med lektier og aktiviteter.
sentence.en: The children get a weekly plan from school with homework and activities.

en ugle.explanation: "En ugle" means "an owl". To say a person stays up late, use "en natugle" (a night owl): "Min bror er en natugle" (My brother is a night owl).

sentence.da: En **ugle** jager om natten.
sentence.en: An owl hunts at night.

en uklarhed.explanation: "En uklarhed" means "a lack of clarity". The start "u-" turns a word into its opposite, as in "en klarhed" (clarity). To say a text can be read in two ways, use "en tvetydighed" (an ambiguity) instead: "Sætningen har en tvetydighed" (The sentence has an ambiguity).

sentence.da: Der er stadig **uklarhed** om, hvem der skal betale.
sentence.en: There is still a lack of clarity about who has to pay.

en uldsweater.explanation: "En uldsweater" means "a wool sweater". It is built from "uld" (wool) and "en sweater" (a sweater). To say a sweater is made of another fabric, change the first part: "en bomuldssweater" (a cotton sweater).

sentence.da: En **uldsweater** holder dig varm, men den kan klø.
sentence.en: A wool sweater keeps you warm, but it can itch.

en ulempe.explanation: "En ulempe" means "a disadvantage". Its opposite is "en fordel" (an advantage), and the two come as a pair. For example, "fordele og ulemper" (advantages and disadvantages).

sentence.da: Den store **ulempe** er, at huset er dyrt.
sentence.en: The big disadvantage is that the house is expensive.

en ultralydsscanning.explanation: "En ultralydsscanning" means "an ultrasound scan". It is built from "ultralyd" (ultrasound) and "en scanning" (a scan). A shorter way to say it is just "en scanning": "Jeg har en scanning i morgen" (I have a scan tomorrow).

sentence.da: Hun skal til **ultralydsscanning**, fordi hun er gravid.
sentence.en: She is going for an ultrasound scan because she is pregnant.

en ulv.explanation: "En ulv" means "a wolf". To say someone gives a false alarm, use "at råbe ulv" (literally, to shout wolf): "Han råber ulv hele tiden" (He cries wolf all the time).

sentence.da: En **ulv** jager sammen med sin flok.
sentence.en: A wolf hunts together with its pack.

en ulykke.explanation: "En ulykke" means "an accident". It also means "misfortune". For example, "Det er en stor ulykke for familien" (It is a great misfortune for the family). The start "u-" turns a word into its opposite, so it is built from "u-" and "lykke" (luck, happiness).

sentence.da: Han blev såret i en **ulykke**.
sentence.en: He was injured in an accident.

en undergang.explanation: "En undergang" means "a downfall". It is literally a going under, like the verb "at gå under" (to perish). To say something big comes to an end, use the verb: "Imperiet gik under" (The empire came to an end).

sentence.da: Romerrigets **undergang** kom efter mange års krige.
sentence.en: The downfall of the Roman Empire came after many years of wars.

en underordnet.explanation: "En underordnet" means "a subordinate". The same word is used for something of lower rank: "en underordnet stilling" (a lower position).

sentence.da: En **underordnet** tager imod ordrer fra en overordnet.
sentence.en: A subordinate takes orders from a superior.

en underskrift.explanation: "En underskrift" means "a signature". It is built from "under" (under) and "skrift" (writing), the writing under a text. To say you sign, use "at skrive under" (literally, to write under): "Jeg skriver under på aftalen" (I sign the agreement).

sentence.da: Sæt din **underskrift** nederst på siden.
sentence.en: Put your signature at the bottom of the page.

en undersøgelse.explanation: "En undersøgelse" means "an examination". To say you go for a check at the doctor, say: "Jeg skal til undersøgelse hos lægen" (I am going for an examination at the doctor). When researchers report findings, it means "a study": "Undersøgelsen viser, at mange sover for lidt" (The study shows that many people sleep too little).

sentence.da: Lægen lavede en grundig **undersøgelse** af mit knæ.
sentence.en: The doctor did a thorough examination of my knee.

en undertekst.explanation: "En undertekst" means "a subtitle". It is built from "under" (under) and "en tekst" (a text). To say a film has subtitles, use the plural: "Filmen har danske undertekster" (The movie has Danish subtitles).

sentence.da: Der er en **undertekst** nederst på skærmen.
sentence.en: There is a subtitle at the bottom of the screen.

en undertrøje.explanation: "En undertrøje" means "an undershirt". The start "under-" means "under", as in "en underkjole" (a slip).

sentence.da: Jeg tager en **undertrøje** på under tøjet, når det er koldt.
sentence.en: I put on an undershirt under my clothes when it is cold.

en underviser.explanation: "En underviser" means "an instructor". It comes from the verb "at undervise" (to teach). To name a person who teaches children at school, use "en lærer" (a teacher) instead: "Min lærer hedder Anne" (My teacher is called Anne).

sentence.da: Vores **underviser** på universitetet er meget dygtig.
sentence.en: Our instructor at the university is very skilled.

en undskyldning.explanation: "En undskyldning" means "an apology". It also means "an excuse", a reason you give for something that went wrong. For example, "Han har altid en undskyldning for at komme for sent" (He always has an excuse for being late).

sentence.da: Jeg skylder dig en **undskyldning** for i går.
sentence.en: I owe you an apology for yesterday.

en undtagelse.explanation: "En undtagelse" means "an exception". To say who or what is left out, use "med undtagelse af" (with the exception of): "Alle kom med undtagelse af Lars" (Everyone came except Lars).

sentence.da: Der er en **undtagelse** fra reglen, når man er syg.
sentence.en: There is an exception to the rule when you are sick.

en uniform.explanation: "En uniform" means "a uniform". To name a uniform for school children, put a word in front: "en skoleuniform" (a school uniform).

sentence.da: Soldater går i **uniform**.
sentence.en: Soldiers wear a uniform.

en union.explanation: "En union" means "a union", as in a group of countries. For example, "Den Europæiske Union" (the European Union). A workers' union is a different word, "en fagforening" (a trade union). For another example, "Jeg er medlem af en fagforening" (I am a member of a trade union).

sentence.da: Danmark er medlem af en **union** sammen med mange andre lande.
sentence.en: Denmark is a member of a union together with many other countries.

en uregelmæssighed.explanation: "En uregelmæssighed" means "an irregularity". It is built from "uregelmæssig" (irregular), the same word as in "uregelmæssige verber" (irregular verbs).

sentence.da: Revisoren fandt en **uregelmæssighed** i regnskabet.
sentence.en: The auditor found an irregularity in the accounts.

en urmager.explanation: "En urmager" means "a watchmaker". It is built from "et ur" (a watch or clock) and "-mager" (maker). The ending "-mager" is also in "en skomager" (a shoemaker).

sentence.da: Min **urmager** kan reparere mit gamle ur.
sentence.en: My watchmaker can repair my old watch.

en urne.explanation: "En urne" means "an urn", as in the container for a person's ashes. A box for votes at an election is "en valgurne" (a ballot box). For example, "Hun lægger sin stemme i valgurnen" (She puts her vote in the ballot box).

sentence.da: Den afdødes aske ligger i en **urne**.
sentence.en: The deceased person's ashes are in an urn.

en usb-nøgle.explanation: "En USB-nøgle" means "a USB stick". Literally it is a USB key, since "en nøgle" means "a key".

sentence.da: Jeg gemmer filerne på en **USB-nøgle**.
sentence.en: I save the files on a USB stick.

en usikkerhed.explanation: "En usikkerhed" means "an uncertainty". The start "u-" turns a word into its opposite, as in "sikker" (sure). To say you feel unsure about yourself, use it with "at føle" (to feel): "Jeg føler usikkerhed, når jeg skal tale foran andre" (I feel uncertain when I have to speak in front of others).

sentence.da: Der er stor **usikkerhed** om, hvad der sker næste år.
sentence.en: There is great uncertainty about what will happen next year.

et udbrud.explanation: "Et udbrud" means "an outbreak". When someone suddenly shows a strong feeling, it means "an outburst", used with "af" (of): "et udbrud af vrede" (an outburst of anger).

sentence.da: Der var et **udbrud** af mæslinger på skolen.
sentence.en: There was an outbreak of measles at the school.

et udbud.explanation: "Et udbud" means "a supply", as in goods on the market. It also means "a tender", when a city or a company asks firms to compete for a job: "Kommunen har sendt byggeriet i udbud" (The municipality has put the construction work out to tender).

sentence.da: Der er et stort **udbud** af lejligheder i byen.
sentence.en: There is a large supply of apartments in the city.

et udbytte.explanation: "Et udbytte" means "a yield or benefit". When a company pays money to the people who own its shares, it means "a dividend": "Firmaet udbetaler et udbytte" (The company pays out a dividend).

sentence.da: Vi fik et stort **udbytte** af kurset.
sentence.en: We got a great benefit from the course.

et udfald.explanation: "Et udfald" means "an outcome". To say which event has the outcome, add "af" (of): "udfaldet af kampen" (the outcome of the match).

sentence.da: Valgets **udfald** er stadig uvist.
sentence.en: The outcome of the election is still unknown.

et udflugtsmål.explanation: "Et udflugtsmål" means "a destination for an outing". It is built from "en udflugt" (an outing) and "et mål" (a goal). In sports, "et mål" also means a goal. For example, "Han scorede et mål" (He scored a goal).

sentence.da: Stranden er et populært **udflugtsmål** om sommeren.
sentence.en: The beach is a popular outing destination in the summer.

et udgangspunkt.explanation: "Et udgangspunkt" means "a starting point". To say you start from something, use "at tage udgangspunkt i" (to start from): "Lad os tage udgangspunkt i tallene" (Let us start from the numbers).

sentence.da: Vi har brug for et fælles **udgangspunkt**, før vi kan diskutere.
sentence.en: We need a common starting point before we can discuss.

et udkast.explanation: "Et udkast" means "a draft". It is built from "ud" (out) and "et kast" (a throw). To ask to see an early version, say: "Må jeg se udkastet?" (May I see the draft?)

sentence.da: Jeg har skrevet et **udkast**, men det er ikke færdigt endnu.
sentence.en: I have written a draft, but it is not finished yet.

et udråbstegn.explanation: "Et udråbstegn" means "an exclamation mark". It is built from "udråb" (an exclamation) and "et tegn" (a sign).

sentence.da: Efter ordet hjælp sætter man et **udråbstegn**.
sentence.en: After the word hjælp (help), you put an exclamation mark.

et udsagn.explanation: "Et udsagn" means "a statement". To say that what someone claims is true, say: "Hans udsagn er sandt" (His statement is true). Do not mix it up with "en udtalelse" (an official statement). For example, "Ministeren gav en udtalelse" (The minister gave a statement).

sentence.da: Politiets undersøgelse viste, at hans **udsagn** var forkert.
sentence.en: The police investigation showed that his statement was wrong.

et udsagnsord.explanation: "Et udsagnsord" means "a verb". It is built from "et udsagn" (a statement) and "et ord" (a word). In a dictionary, a verb is listed with "at" (to) in front. For example, "at spise" (to eat).

sentence.da: Et **udsagnsord** fortæller, hvad man gør.
sentence.en: A verb tells what one does.

et udsalg.explanation: "Et udsalg" means "a sale". To say a store has a sale, use it with "at have" (to have): "Butikken har udsalg" (The store has a sale). To talk about one item at a special price, use "et tilbud" (an offer) instead: "Der er tilbud på mælk" (Milk is on offer).

sentence.da: Jakken er billig på **udsalg**.
sentence.en: The jacket is cheap on sale.

et udseende.explanation: "Et udseende" means "an appearance". It comes from the verb "at se ud" (to look). To describe how someone looks, use the verb: "Hun ser træt ud" (She looks tired).

sentence.da: Man skal ikke dømme folk på deres **udseende**.
sentence.en: You should not judge people by their looks.

et udsigtspunkt.explanation: "Et udsigtspunkt" means "a viewpoint". It is built from "en udsigt" (a view) and "et punkt" (a point).

sentence.da: Fra et **udsigtspunkt** på bakken kan man se hele byen.
sentence.en: From a viewpoint on the hill you can see the whole city.

et udslip.explanation: "Et udslip" means "a leak". For a spill of oil, put a word in front: "et olieudslip" (an oil spill).

sentence.da: Et **udslip** af olie kan skade havet og dyrene.
sentence.en: A spill of oil can harm the sea and the animals.

et udslæt.explanation: "Et udslæt" means "a rash". To say someone got a rash, you can leave out "et": "Han fik udslæt" (He got a rash).

sentence.da: Jeg fik et **udslæt** på huden, fordi jeg er allergisk.
sentence.en: I got a rash on my skin because I am allergic.

et udspil.explanation: "Et udspil" means "a proposal". In card games, it means the first card played. For example, "Hvem har udspillet?" (Who has the lead?)

sentence.da: Regeringen har lagt et nyt **udspil** frem om skatten.
sentence.en: The government has put forward a new proposal about taxes.

et udtryk.explanation: "Et udtryk" means "an expression". When you talk about the look on someone's face, put "ansigts-" (face) in front: "et ansigtsudtryk" (a facial expression).

sentence.da: Det er et gammelt dansk **udtryk**.
sentence.en: That is an old Danish expression.

et uheld.explanation: "Et uheld" means "an accident or bad luck". To say something happened by mistake, use "ved et uheld" (by accident): "Glasset gik i stykker ved et uheld" (The glass broke by accident). A serious crash with injuries is "en ulykke" (an accident). For example, "Der var en ulykke på motorvejen" (There was an accident on the highway).

sentence.da: Det var et **uheld**, undskyld.
sentence.en: It was an accident, sorry.

et underholdningsprogram.explanation: "Et underholdningsprogram" means "an entertainment show". It is built from "underholdning" (entertainment) and "et program" (a program).

sentence.da: Et **underholdningsprogram** er lavet, så folk kan more sig.
sentence.en: An entertainment show is made so that people can have fun.

et underskud.explanation: "Et underskud" means "a deficit". Its opposite is "et overskud" (a surplus). For example, "Firmaet har et overskud" (The company has a surplus). When you say you have energy left for other people or tasks, you also use "overskud": "Jeg har ikke overskud i dag" (I have no energy to spare today).

sentence.da: Firmaet har et **underskud**, fordi udgifterne er for store.
sentence.en: The company has a deficit because the costs are too big.

et ungdomshus.explanation: "Et ungdomshus" means "a youth center". It is built from "ungdom" (youth) and "et hus" (a house).

sentence.da: Der er et **ungdomshus** i byen, hvor unge kan mødes.
sentence.en: There is a youth center in town where young people can meet.

et ungdomskort.explanation: "Et ungdomskort" means "a youth travel pass". It is built from "ungdom" (youth) and "et kort" (a card). "Et kort" also means a map. For example, "et kort over byen" (a map of the city).

sentence.da: Med et **ungdomskort** er toget meget billigere.
sentence.en: With a youth travel pass, the train is much cheaper.

et univers.explanation: "Et univers" means "a universe". To talk about the whole world of an author or a film, use it for that world: "forfatterens univers" (the author's universe).

sentence.da: Vores sol er kun én stjerne i et stort **univers**.
sentence.en: Our sun is only one star in a big universe.

et universitet.explanation: "Et universitet" means "a university". To say you study a subject there, use "at læse" (to read): "Jeg læser biologi" (I study biology).

sentence.da: Min søster læser på et **universitet** i Aarhus.
sentence.en: My sister studies at a university in Aarhus.

et upload.explanation: "Et upload" means "an upload". It comes from the verb "at uploade" (to upload). To say you do it, use the verb: "Jeg uploader filen" (I upload the file).

sentence.da: Dit **upload** tager lang tid, fordi filen er stor.
sentence.en: Your upload takes a long time because the file is big.

et ur.explanation: "Et ur" means "a clock or watch". To say a watch you wear on your wrist, use "et armbåndsur" (a wristwatch): "Jeg har et armbåndsur på" (I am wearing a wristwatch). Do not mix it up with "klokken" (o'clock), which is used for telling the time: "Hvad er klokken?" (What time is it?)

sentence.da: Mit **ur** viser klokken ti.
sentence.en: My watch shows ten o'clock.

uacceptabel.explanation: "Uacceptabel" means "unacceptable". It is built from "u-" (not) and "acceptabel" (acceptable). To say a result is not good enough, use it before the noun: "et uacceptabelt resultat" (an unacceptable result).

sentence.da: Det er **uacceptabel** opførsel at slå en anden.
sentence.en: It is unacceptable behavior to hit someone.

uafgjort.explanation: "Uafgjort" means "tied", as in a game where both sides have the same score. It is built from "u-" (not) and "afgjort" (decided), so literally it is undecided.

sentence.da: Kampen endte **uafgjort**.
sentence.en: The match ended in a draw.

uafhængig.explanation: "Uafhængig" means "independent". It is built from "u-" (not) and "afhængig" (dependent). To say who you are independent of, add "af" (of): "Hun er uafhængig af sine forældre" (She is independent of her parents).

sentence.da: En **uafhængig** avis tager ikke penge fra politiske partier.
sentence.en: An independent newspaper does not take money from political parties.

uafhængighed.explanation: "Uafhængighed" means "independence". It is built from "uafhængig" (independent) and the ending "-hed". To describe a person, use "uafhængig" instead: "Hun er uafhængig" (She is independent).

sentence.da: Landet fik sin **uafhængighed**, og nu bestemmer det selv.
sentence.en: The country got its independence, and now it decides for itself.

uanset.explanation: "Uanset" means "no matter". Before a noun it means "regardless of". For example, "uanset alder" (regardless of age). Before a question word it means "no matter what". For another example, "uanset hvad" (no matter what).

sentence.da: Vi spiller fodbold hver søndag, **uanset** om det regner.
sentence.en: We play soccer every Sunday regardless of whether it rains.

uanstændig.explanation: "Uanstændig" means "indecent". It is built from "u-" (not) and "anstændig" (decent). For a different use, say prices are far too high: "uanstændigt høje priser" (indecently high prices).

sentence.da: Det er **uanstændig** opførsel at råbe af en gammel dame.
sentence.en: It is indecent behavior to shout at an old lady.

uansvarlig.explanation: "Uansvarlig" means "irresponsible". It is built from "u-" (not) and "ansvarlig" (responsible). To call an action irresponsible, use it after "det er" (it is): "Det er uansvarligt at køre så hurtigt" (It is irresponsible to drive that fast).

sentence.da: Det var en **uansvarlig** beslutning at lade børnene være alene.
sentence.en: It was an irresponsible decision to leave the children alone.

uartig.explanation: "Uartig" means "naughty". It is built from "u-" (not) and "artig" (well-behaved). To tell a child they have been naughty: "Du har været uartig" (You have been naughty).

sentence.da: Hunden var **uartig** og tyggede på sofaen.
sentence.en: The dog was naughty and chewed on the sofa.

ubegribelig.explanation: "Ubegribelig" means "incomprehensible". It is built from "u-" (not), "at begribe" (to grasp) and "-elig" (can be), so literally it cannot be grasped. To say something makes no sense to you: "Det er mig ubegribeligt" (I cannot understand it).

sentence.da: Jeg finder hans handling **ubegribelig**, fordi den ikke giver mening.
sentence.en: I find his action incomprehensible because it makes no sense.

ubehagelig.explanation: "Ubehagelig" means "unpleasant". It is built from "u-" (not) and "behagelig" (pleasant). To describe a person you do not like being around: "en ubehagelig person" (an unpleasant person). To say a situation feels awkward, it also means "uncomfortable": "Det er ubehageligt" (It is uncomfortable).

sentence.da: En **ubehagelig** lugt kom fra køkkenet.
sentence.en: An unpleasant smell came from the kitchen.

ubekymret.explanation: "Ubekymret" means "carefree". It is built from "u-" (not) and "bekymret" (worried). To describe a childhood without worries: "en ubekymret barndom" (a carefree childhood).

sentence.da: Som barn levede hun et **ubekymret** liv uden regninger.
sentence.en: As a child she lived a carefree life without bills.

ubelejlig.explanation: "Ubelejlig" means "inconvenient". It is built from "u-" (not) and "belejlig" (convenient). To ask whether you are interrupting someone, say: "Kommer jeg ubelejligt?" (Is this a bad time?)

sentence.da: Det er en **ubelejlig** tid at ringe på, fordi vi spiser.
sentence.en: It is an inconvenient time to ring the doorbell, because we are eating.

ubestemt.explanation: "Ubestemt" means "vague". It is built from "u-" (not) and "bestemt" (specific). To describe a feeling you cannot name: "en ubestemt følelse" (a vague feeling). To say something has no end date, use "på ubestemt tid" (for an unspecified time).

sentence.da: Han gav kun et **ubestemt** svar på spørgsmålet.
sentence.en: He only gave a vague answer to the question.

ubestemt form.explanation: "Ubestemt form" means "indefinite form". To put a noun in this form, say it with "en" or "et" before it: "en bil" (a car), "et hus" (a house). The form with "the" adds an ending. For example, "bilen" (the car).

sentence.da: En hund og et hus står i **ubestemt form**.
sentence.en: A dog and a house are in the indefinite form.

ubetydelig.explanation: "Ubetydelig" means "insignificant". It is built from "u-" (not) and "betydelig" (significant). To say damage is too small to matter: "Skaden er ubetydelig" (The damage is insignificant).

sentence.da: Forskellen mellem de to priser er **ubetydelig**, kun to kroner.
sentence.en: The difference between the two prices is insignificant, only two kroner.

ubevæbnet.explanation: "Ubevæbnet" means "unarmed". It is built from "u-" (not) and "bevæbnet" (armed). To describe a guard with no weapon: "en ubevæbnet vagt" (an unarmed guard).

sentence.da: Betjenten var **ubevæbnet** og bar kun en lommelygte.
sentence.en: The officer was unarmed and only carried a flashlight.

ubrugelig.explanation: "Ubrugelig" means "useless". The opposite is "brugbar" (usable). To say what something is useless for, add "til" (for): "Den er ubrugelig til dette" (It is useless for this).

sentence.da: Den gamle telefon er helt **ubrugelig**.
sentence.en: The old phone is completely useless.

ud.explanation: "Ud" means "out" and is used for going from inside to outside: "Vi går ud" (We go out). To name the place where you are, Danish uses "ude" (outside): "Vi er ude" (We are outside). "Ud" is also part of "se ud" (to look, to appear). For example, "Hvordan ser det ud?" (What does it look like?)

forms.en: He goes out of the house.
I go out into the garden.

sentence.da: Vi går **ud** i haven.
sentence.en: We go out into the garden.

ud over.explanation: "Ud over" means "besides". To add one more thing to what you already named: "Ud over kaffe har vi te" (Besides coffee, we have tea). It is built from "ud" (out) and "over" (over). The spelling "udover" also exists.

sentence.da: **Ud over** mig kommer der to andre gæster.
sentence.en: Besides me, two other guests are coming.

ud over det.explanation: "Ud over det" means "besides that". To add one more point to what you just said: "Ud over det er det for dyrt" (Besides that, it is too expensive). It is built from "ud over" (besides) and "det" (that).

forms.da: Ud over det er alt fint.
Ud over det har jeg ingen planer.
forms.en: Besides that, I have no plans.

sentence.da: Jeg har ondt i hovedet, og **ud over det** er jeg træt.
sentence.en: I have a headache, and besides that I am tired.

udadvendt.explanation: "Udadvendt" means "outgoing". Literally it means "turned outward". The opposite is "indadvendt" (withdrawn, quiet), literally "turned inward". For example, "Han er indadvendt og siger ikke meget" (He is withdrawn and does not say much).

sentence.da: Hun er **udadvendt** og får nemt nye venner.
sentence.en: She is outgoing and easily makes new friends.

uddannet.explanation: "Uddannet" means "qualified", as in having finished the training for a job. To say which job, say it right after: "Hun er uddannet tømrer" (She is a trained carpenter). It also means "educated". For example, "Hun er højt uddannet" (She is highly educated).

sentence.da: Han er **uddannet** sygeplejerske og arbejder på et hospital.
sentence.en: He is a trained nurse and works at a hospital.

ude af øje, ude af sind.explanation: "Ude af øje, ude af sind" means "out of sight, out of mind". Literally, it is "out of eye, out of mind". "Ude af" means "out of" in other phrases too. For example, "ude af kontrol" (out of control).

forms.da: Ude af øje, ude af sind, siger man.
forms.en: Out of sight, out of mind, as they say.

sentence.da: Han flyttede til udlandet, og nu er det **ude af øje, ude af sind**.
sentence.en: He moved abroad, and now it is out of sight, out of mind.

udefra.explanation: "Udefra" means "from outside". It is built from "ude" (outside) and "fra" (from). To say you look at something as an outsider: "Set udefra ser det nemt ud" (Seen from outside, it looks easy).

sentence.da: Larmen kommer **udefra**, og vinduet står åbent.
sentence.en: The noise comes from outside, and the window is open.

udelukkende.explanation: "Udelukkende" means "only". It comes from the verb "at udelukke" (to exclude), so it means everything else is left out. To say a shop sells one kind of food and nothing else: "Butikken sælger udelukkende økologisk mad" (The shop sells only organic food).

sentence.da: Suppen består **udelukkende** af grøntsager og vand.
sentence.en: The soup consists only of vegetables and water.

udelukket.explanation: "Udelukket" means "excluded". It comes from the verb "at udelukke" (to exclude). To say something cannot happen, use "Det er udelukket" (It is out of the question) as a firm answer to a suggestion.

forms.en: It is almost out of the question.

sentence.da: Hun blev **udelukket** fra konkurrencen, fordi hun snød.
sentence.en: She was excluded from the competition because she cheated.

uden.explanation: "Uden" means "without", the opposite of "med" (with). For example, "kaffe med mælk" (coffee with milk), "kaffe uden mælk" (coffee without milk). To say you do without doing something, add "at" before the action word: "uden at spise" (without eating).

sentence.da: Jeg vil have kaffe **uden** sukker.
sentence.en: I want coffee without sugar.

uden tvivl.explanation: "Uden tvivl" means "without a doubt". It is built from "uden" (without) and "tvivl" (doubt). To agree strongly with a question: "Er det en god idé?" "Uden tvivl!" (Is it a good idea? Without a doubt!)

forms.en: It is without a doubt good.
She will win without a doubt.

sentence.da: Det er **uden tvivl** den bedste kage.
sentence.en: It is without a doubt the best cake.

udenad.explanation: "Udenad" means "by heart". To say you learn something by heart, use "at lære noget udenad" (to learn something by heart).

forms.en: to know the song by heart
to recite the poem by heart
She knows the tables by heart

sentence.da: Skuespilleren kan sin rolle **udenad** og behøver ikke noget manuskript.
sentence.en: The actor knows her role by heart and does not need a script.

udenfor.explanation: "Udenfor" means "outside". To say where someone is: "Hunden sover udenfor" (The dog sleeps outside). To say where someone goes: "Vi går udenfor" (We go outside).

sentence.da: Børnene leger **udenfor** i haven.
sentence.en: The children play outside in the garden.

udenlands.explanation: "Udenlands" means "abroad" and names where you are or where you go. For example, "Hun bor udenlands" (She lives abroad). Do not mix it up with "udenlandsk" (foreign), which describes a thing. For another example, "en udenlandsk bil" (a foreign car).

sentence.da: Hun har studeret **udenlands** i to år.
sentence.en: She has studied abroad for two years.

udenlandsk.explanation: "Udenlandsk" means "foreign". Do not mix it up with "udenlands" (abroad), which says where someone goes or is: "Hun bor udenlands" (She lives abroad).

sentence.da: Min far arbejder for et **udenlandsk** firma.
sentence.en: My father works for a foreign company.

udholdenhed.explanation: "En udholdenhed" means "endurance". It is built from "at holde ud" (to hold out, to endure) and the ending "-hed".

sentence.da: Maratonløb kræver stor **udholdenhed**, fordi man løber i mange timer.
sentence.en: Marathon running requires great endurance because you run for many hours.

udkig.explanation: "Et udkig" means "lookout", as in a high place to look from. To say you are searching for something, use "på udkig efter" (on the lookout for): "Jeg er på udkig efter en lejlighed" (I am on the lookout for an apartment). Do not mix it up with "en udsigt" (a view), which is what you see. For example, "Der er en flot udsigt" (There is a nice view).

sentence.da: Fra det høje **udkig** kunne vi se hele byen.
sentence.en: From the high lookout we could see the whole city.

udlændingepolitik.explanation: "En udlændingepolitik" means "an immigration policy". It is built from "udlændinge" (foreigners) and "politik" (policy), so literally it is a foreigner policy.

sentence.da: Regler om visum og ophold hører til **udlændingepolitik**.
sentence.en: Rules about visas and residence belong to immigration policy.

udmattet.explanation: "Udmattet" means "exhausted". It comes from the verb "at udmatte" (to wear out). Do not mix it up with "træt" (tired), which is milder. For example, "Jeg er træt" (I am tired) and "Jeg er udmattet" (I am exhausted).

sentence.da: Hun var **udmattet** efter maratonløbet og kunne næsten ikke gå.
sentence.en: She was exhausted after the marathon and could hardly walk.

udmærket.explanation: "Udmærket" means "excellent". As a reply that agrees to a suggestion, it also means "fine": "Kan vi mødes klokken ti?" "Udmærket!" (Can we meet at ten? Fine!)

sentence.da: Det er et **udmærket** sted at bo.
sentence.en: It is an excellent place to live.

udover.explanation: "Udover" means "besides", adding something to what you already named. It can also mean "beyond". For example, "udover det sædvanlige" (beyond the usual). The two-word spelling "ud over" also exists.

sentence.da: **Udover** dansk taler hun også engelsk.
sentence.en: Besides Danish, she also speaks English.

udsat.explanation: "Udsat" means "vulnerable", as in a group open to harm. For example, "en udsat gruppe" (a vulnerable group). When something is open to a danger, it means "exposed", with "for" (to): "udsat for kulde" (exposed to cold). When something is moved to a later time, it means "postponed": "Mødet er udsat" (The meeting is postponed).

sentence.da: Fyret ligger helt ude i havet og er **udsat** for storm.
sentence.en: The lighthouse lies far out in the sea and is exposed to storms.

udsolgt.explanation: "Udsolgt" means "sold out". It is built from "ud" (out) and "solgt" (sold). To say a show has no tickets left: "Koncerten er udsolgt" (The concert is sold out).

sentence.da: Der er ingen billetter. De er **udsolgt**.
sentence.en: There are no tickets. They are sold out.

udstyr.explanation: "Udstyr" means "equipment". This word has no article, so leave out "et". For example, "Jeg har mit eget udstyr med" (I have my own equipment with me).

sentence.da: Vi har telt og andet **udstyr** med.
sentence.en: We brought a tent and other equipment.

uduelig.explanation: "Uduelig" means "incompetent". It is built from "u-" (not) and "duelig" (capable), so literally it is not capable.

sentence.da: Han blev fyret, fordi han var **uduelig** som chef.
sentence.en: He was fired because he was incompetent as a boss.

udødelig.explanation: "Udødelig" means "immortal". It is built from "u-" (not) and "dødelig" (mortal). To say a work will be remembered forever, use it for the work: "Shakespeares værker er udødelige" (Shakespeare's works are immortal).

sentence.da: I myten var guden **udødelig** og kunne aldrig dø.
sentence.en: In the myth the god was immortal and could never die.

uendelig.explanation: "Uendelig" means "endless". It is built from "u-" (not) and "endelig" (final). To make a feeling stronger, put it before the feeling word: "Jeg er uendelig taknemmelig" (I am endlessly grateful).

sentence.da: Ventetiden føltes **uendelig**, fordi vi frøs i kulden.
sentence.en: The wait felt endless because we were freezing in the cold.

uenig.explanation: "Uenig" means "in disagreement" and is used for people who do not think the same: "Vi er uenige" (We disagree). To say with whom, add "med" (with): "Jeg er uenig med dig" (I disagree with you). To say about what, add "om" (about): "uenig om prisen" (in disagreement about the price).

sentence.da: Jeg er **uenig** med dig i det.
sentence.en: I disagree with you on that.

uerfaren.explanation: "Uerfaren" means "inexperienced". It is built from "u-" (not) and "erfaren" (experienced).

sentence.da: Han er **uerfaren** og har aldrig kørt på motorvej.
sentence.en: He is inexperienced and has never driven on a highway.

ufattelig.explanation: "Ufattelig" means "unthinkable". It is built from "u-" (not), "at fatte" (to grasp) and "-elig" (can be), so literally it cannot be grasped. When something is far bigger than you expected, it also means "incredible": "et ufatteligt tal" (an incredible number). To make a word stronger, put it before that word: "ufattelig smuk" (unbelievably beautiful).

sentence.da: Han tabte en **ufattelig** sum penge på én aften.
sentence.en: He lost an incredible sum of money in one evening.

uforglemmelig.explanation: "Uforglemmelig" means "unforgettable". It is built from "u-" (not) and "-elig" (can be) around the verb "at glemme" (to forget), so literally it cannot be forgotten. To describe something you lived through: "en uforglemmelig oplevelse" (an unforgettable experience).

sentence.da: Hun gav os en **uforglemmelig** aften med god mad og musik.
sentence.en: She gave us an unforgettable evening with good food and music.

uformel.explanation: "Uformel" means "informal". It is built from "u-" (not) and "formel" (formal). To describe clothes that are not smart: "uformelt tøj" (informal clothes).

sentence.da: Til en **uformel** middag må man gerne komme i jeans.
sentence.en: At an informal dinner you may come in jeans.

uforskammet.explanation: "Uforskammet" means "rude". To say a price is shockingly high, put it before the price word: "uforskammet dyrt" (outrageously expensive).

sentence.da: Det var **uforskammet** af ham at svare sin mor sådan.
sentence.en: It was impertinent of him to answer his mother like that.

uforudsigelig.explanation: "Uforudsigelig" means "unpredictable". It is built from "u-" (not) and "forudsigelig" (predictable).

sentence.da: En **uforudsigelig** hund kan skifte humør på et sekund.
sentence.en: An unpredictable dog can change mood in a second.

ugen efter.explanation: "Ugen efter" means "the week after". To say something happened in the week after a party: "Ugen efter festen var jeg syg" (The week after the party I was sick). For the day after, use "dagen efter": "Dagen efter rejste hun" (The day after, she left).

sentence.da: Jeg er tilbage på arbejde **ugen efter** ferien.
sentence.en: I am back at work the week after the vacation.

ugevis.explanation: "Ugevis" means "for weeks". It is built from "en uge" (a week) and the ending "-vis", which gives the meaning "week after week". To say you waited a long time: "Vi ventede ugevis" (We waited for weeks).

sentence.da: Når noget varer **ugevis**, tæller man ikke længere dagene.
sentence.en: When something lasts for weeks, you stop counting the days.

ugift.explanation: "Ugift" means "unmarried". It is built from "u-" (not) and "gift" (married). The same "u-" is in "uvenlig" (unfriendly), the opposite of "venlig" (friendly).

sentence.da: Han er **ugift** og har ingen kone.
sentence.en: He is unmarried and has no wife.

ugyldig.explanation: "Ugyldig" means "invalid". It is built from "u-" (not) and "gyldig" (valid). To say a code cannot be used: "Koden er ugyldig" (The code is invalid).

sentence.da: Billetten er **ugyldig**, fordi datoen er passeret.
sentence.en: The ticket is invalid because the date has passed.

uha.explanation: "Uha" means "oh dear" and shows worry or unease. For example, "Uha, det ser dyrt ud!" (Oh dear, that looks expensive!)

sentence.da: **Uha**, det her ser svært ud.
sentence.en: Oh dear, this looks hard.

uheldig.explanation: "Uheldig" means "unlucky". It is built from "u-" (not) and "heldig" (lucky). When something turns out badly, it means "unfortunate": "en uheldig bemærkning" (an unfortunate remark).

sentence.da: Jeg var **uheldig** og mistede min nøgle i går.
sentence.en: I was unlucky and lost my key yesterday.

uhyggelig.explanation: "Uhyggelig" means "creepy". It is built from "u-" (not) and "hyggelig" (cozy). To say a place gives you the creeps: "Huset er uhyggeligt" (The house is creepy).

sentence.da: Skoven er mørk og **uhyggelig** om natten.
sentence.en: The forest is dark and creepy at night.

uhyre.explanation: "Uhyre" means "immensely". To make an adjective stronger, put it before the adjective: "uhyre vigtig" (immensely important). As a noun, it takes "et" and means a monster. For example, "et uhyre" (a monster).

sentence.da: Eventyret handler om et **uhyre** med tre hoveder.
sentence.en: The fairy tale is about a monster with three heads.

uhøflig.explanation: "Uhøflig" means "rude". It is built from "u-" (not) and "høflig" (polite). To say who someone is rude to, add "mod" (to): "Vær ikke uhøflig mod din lærer" (Do not be rude to your teacher).

sentence.da: Han var meget **uhøflig** mod tjeneren.
sentence.en: He was very rude to the waiter.

ukendt.explanation: "Ukendt" means "unknown". It is built from "u-" (not) and "kendt" (known). To say you do not know someone: "Han er ukendt for mig" (He is unknown to me).

sentence.da: Brevet kom fra en **ukendt** afsender.
sentence.en: The letter came from an unknown sender.

ukraine.explanation: "Ukraine" means "Ukraine". To say where you are, use "i" (in): "Jeg bor i Ukraine" (I live in Ukraine). To say where you go, use "til" (to): "Vi rejser til Ukraine" (We travel to Ukraine).

sentence.da: Kyiv er en stor by i **Ukraine**.
sentence.en: Kyiv is a big city in Ukraine.

ukrainsk.explanation: "Ukrainsk" means "Ukrainian". It is built from "Ukraine" (Ukraine) and the ending "-sk". English writes "Ukrainian" starting with U, but Danish writes "ukrainsk" starting with u.

sentence.da: Hun kommer fra Ukraine og taler **ukrainsk**.
sentence.en: She comes from Ukraine and speaks Ukrainian.

ukrudt.explanation: "Ukrudt" means "weeds". This word has no article, so leave out "et". For example, "Der er meget ukrudt i haven" (There are a lot of weeds in the garden).

sentence.da: Vi fjernede **ukrudt** fra bedene, så blomsterne fik plads.
sentence.en: We removed weeds from the beds so the flowers got room.

uld.explanation: "Uld" means "wool". This word has no article. To say what something is made of, use "af" (of): "Sokkerne er af uld" (The socks are made of wool).

sentence.da: Jeg vil have en trøje af **uld**, fordi den er varm.
sentence.en: I want a sweater made of wool because it is warm.

ulige.explanation: "Ulige" means "odd", as in an odd number such as 3 or 7. It is built from "u-" (not) and "lige" (even). For a different use, it means "unequal": "en ulige kamp" (an unequal fight).

sentence.da: Tallene tre og fem er **ulige**, men fire er lige.
sentence.en: The numbers three and five are odd, but four is even.

ulovlig.explanation: "Ulovlig" means "illegal". It is built from "u-" (not) and "lovlig" (legal). To say the law forbids something: "Det er ulovligt at parkere her" (It is illegal to park here).

sentence.da: En **ulovlig** handling kan give en bøde.
sentence.en: An illegal act can lead to a fine.

ultimativ.explanation: "Ultimativ" means "ultimate", as in the best or most extreme of its kind. It also means "final", as in a demand that leaves no room to negotiate. For example, "et ultimativt krav" (a final demand).

sentence.da: Et maratonløb er en **ultimativ** test af, hvor meget man kan holde ud.
sentence.en: A marathon is the ultimate test of how much you can endure.

ulydig.explanation: "Ulydig" means "disobedient". It is built from "u-" (not) and "lydig" (obedient).

sentence.da: Hunden er **ulydig** og kommer ikke, når jeg kalder.
sentence.en: The dog is disobedient and does not come when I call.

ulykkelig.explanation: "Ulykkelig" means "unhappy". It is built from "u-" (not) and "lykkelig" (happy). To say someone is unhappy because of an event: "Han er ulykkelig efter bruddet" (He is unhappy after the breakup).

sentence.da: Hun var **ulykkelig**, fordi hun savnede sin familie.
sentence.en: She was unhappy because she missed her family.

ulækker.explanation: "Ulækker" means "disgusting". Its opposite is "lækker" (tasty, nice). For example, "Kagen er lækker" (The cake is tasty).

sentence.da: Den gamle mælk er **ulækker**, og jeg drikker den ikke.
sentence.en: The old milk is disgusting, and I do not drink it.

umiddelbart.explanation: "Umiddelbart" means "at first sight", before you look closer. When you put it in front of "efter" (after), it means "right": "umiddelbart efter mødet" (right after the meeting).

forms.en: At first sight it seems fine

sentence.da: **Umiddelbart** ser huset pænt ud, men taget er gammelt.
sentence.en: At first sight the house looks nice, but the roof is old.

umoden.explanation: "Umoden" means "immature". It is built from "u-" (not) and "moden" (ripe, grown-up). For fruit that is not ready to eat, it means "unripe": "et umodent æble" (an unripe apple).

sentence.da: Den grønne pære er **umoden**, så den smager surt.
sentence.en: The green pear is unripe, so it tastes sour.

umulig.explanation: "Umulig" means "impossible". It is built from "u-" (not) and "mulig" (possible). When you say a person is hard to deal with, it also means "impossible" in that sense: "Du er umulig!" (You are impossible!)

sentence.da: Det er en **umulig** opgave på én dag.
sentence.en: It is an impossible task in one day.

under.explanation: "Under" means "under". To say where something is, use it before a place: "Katten sover under sengen" (The cat sleeps under the bed). To say when something happens, it means "during": "under ferien" (during the holiday). Before a number, it means "less than". For example, "under ti" (under ten).

sentence.da: Katten sover **under** sengen.
sentence.en: The cat sleeps under the bed.

under alle omstændigheder.explanation: "Under alle omstændigheder" means "in any case". It is built from "under" (under), "alle" (all) and "omstændigheder" (circumstances), so literally it is under all circumstances. To say something must never happen, use "under ingen omstændigheder" (under no circumstances): "Det må under ingen omstændigheder ske" (It must not happen under any circumstances).

forms.en: I am coming in any case

forms.da: Det skal ske under alle omstændigheder
forms.en: It must happen no matter what

forms.da: under alle omstændigheder skal du ringe
forms.en: in any case you must call

sentence.da: Vi skal **under alle omstændigheder** nå flyet i morgen.
sentence.en: We must catch the plane tomorrow no matter what.

underbukser.explanation: "Underbukser" means "underpants". It is built from "under" (under) and "bukser" (pants). To say one item, use "et par" (a pair of): "et par underbukser" (a pair of underpants).

sentence.da: Jeg har **underbukser** på under bukserne.
sentence.en: I wear underpants under my pants.

underholdende.explanation: "Underholdende" means "entertaining". It comes from the verb "at underholde" (to entertain). To say how a show was: "Showet var meget underholdende" (The show was very entertaining).

sentence.da: Bogen er **underholdende**, så jeg læste den på én dag.
sentence.en: The book is entertaining, so I read it in one day.

underholdning.explanation: "En underholdning" means "entertainment". It comes from the verb "at underholde" (to entertain). To say a place offers it for free: "Der er gratis underholdning" (There is free entertainment).

sentence.da: Musik og dans er god **underholdning** til festen.
sentence.en: Music and dance are good entertainment for the party.

underlig.explanation: "Underlig" means "weird". To say you find something odd: "Det er underligt, at han ikke ringer" (It is weird that he does not call).

sentence.da: Min nabo er **underlig**, fordi han aldrig taler.
sentence.en: My neighbor is strange because he never talks.

undertøj.explanation: "Undertøj" means "underwear". It is built from "under" (under) and "tøj" (clothes). This word has no article, so leave out "et". For example, "Jeg har købt nyt undertøj" (I bought new underwear).

sentence.da: Man har **undertøj** på under tøjet.
sentence.en: You wear underwear under your clothes.

undervejs.explanation: "Undervejs" means "along the way". To say something has not arrived yet: "Pakken er undervejs" (The package is on its way). To say where you are heading, use "på vej" (on the way) with "til" (to): "på vej til skolen" (on the way to school).

forms.en: The package is on its way
I learn a lot along the way

sentence.da: Vi spiste frokost **undervejs**, fordi turen var lang.
sentence.en: We ate lunch along the way because the trip was long.
