undervisning.explanation: "Undervisning" means "teaching", as in lessons at a school. To say when the lessons start: "Undervisningen begynder klokken otte" (Classes begin at eight).

sentence.da: Læreren giver **undervisning** i dansk hver mandag.
sentence.en: The teacher gives Danish lessons every Monday.

undskyld.explanation: "Undskyld" means "sorry or excuse me". To apologize: "Undskyld, jeg kom for sent" (Sorry, I came too late). To get someone's attention politely: "Undskyld, må jeg komme forbi?" (Excuse me, may I get past?). To ask someone to repeat because you did not hear, say "Undskyld?" (Pardon?)

forms.en: Excuse me, where is the station?

sentence.da: **Undskyld**, hvor er toilettet?
sentence.en: Excuse me, where is the toilet?

undskyld mig.explanation: "Undskyld mig" means "excuse me". It is built from "undskyld" (sorry) and "mig" (me). To get someone's attention: "Undskyld mig, hvor er stationen?" (Excuse me, where is the station?)

forms.en: Excuse me, where is the station?

sentence.da: **Undskyld mig**, må jeg komme forbi?
sentence.en: Excuse me, may I get past?

undtagen.explanation: "Undtagen" means "except". It comes from the verb "at undtage" (to make an exception). To say a rule has an exception: "Reglen gælder for alle undtagen børn" (The rule applies to everyone except children).

sentence.da: Alle kom, **undtagen** min bror.
sentence.en: Everyone came, except my brother.

undvigende.explanation: "Undvigende" means "evasive". It comes from the verb "at undvige" (to dodge).

sentence.da: Han var **undvigende**, da jeg spurgte, hvor han havde været.
sentence.en: He was evasive when I asked where he had been.

ung.explanation: "Ung" means "young". To talk about young people in general, say "de unge" (the young): "De unge bruger telefonen meget" (Young people use the phone a lot).

sentence.da: Hun er femten år. Hun er **ung**.
sentence.en: She is fifteen years old. She is young.

ungdom.explanation: "Ungdom" means "youth". It is built from "ung" (young) and the ending "-dom", which is also in "sygdom" (illness), from "syg" (sick).

sentence.da: I min **ungdom** spillede jeg meget fodbold.
sentence.en: In my youth I played a lot of soccer.

unik.explanation: "Unik" means "unique". To say a chance is rare and special: "Det er en unik chance" (It is a unique chance).

sentence.da: Din stemme er **unik**, fordi ingen andre lyder som dig.
sentence.en: Your voice is unique because no one else sounds like you.

unødvendig.explanation: "Unødvendig" means "unnecessary". It is built from "u-" (not) and "nødvendig" (necessary). To say something can be skipped: "Det er unødvendigt at betale to gange" (It is unnecessary to pay twice).

sentence.da: Din bekymring er **unødvendig**, fordi alt er i orden.
sentence.en: Your worry is unnecessary because everything is fine.

uovervindelig.explanation: "Uovervindelig" means "invincible". It is built from "u-" (not), "at overvinde" (to overcome) and "-elig" (can be), so literally it cannot be overcome. The same "-elig" is in "ubegribelig" (incomprehensible).

sentence.da: Hæren virkede **uovervindelig**, fordi den aldrig havde tabt.
sentence.en: The army seemed invincible because it had never lost.

upassende.explanation: "Upassende" means "inappropriate". It is built from "u-" (not) and "passende" (suitable). To say clothes do not suit an event: "upassende tøj til en begravelse" (inappropriate clothes for a funeral).

sentence.da: Det er **upassende** at bære festtøj til en begravelse.
sentence.en: It is inappropriate to wear party clothes to a funeral.

upopulær.explanation: "Upopulær" means "unpopular". It is built from "u-" (not) and "populær" (popular). To say a decision upsets many people: "en upopulær beslutning" (an unpopular decision).

sentence.da: Den nye regel er **upopulær**, og mange klager.
sentence.en: The new rule is unpopular, and many people complain.

upraktisk.explanation: "Upraktisk" means "impractical". It is built from "u-" (not) and "praktisk" (handy). To say shoes are hard to use: "Skoene er upraktiske" (The shoes are impractical).

sentence.da: En hvid sofa er **upraktisk**, når man har små børn.
sentence.en: A white sofa is impractical when you have small children.

upålidelig.explanation: "Upålidelig" means "unreliable". It is built from "u-" (not) and "pålidelig" (dependable). To say a source cannot be trusted: "Kilden er upålidelig" (The source is unreliable).

sentence.da: Han er **upålidelig**, fordi han ofte kommer for sent.
sentence.en: He is unreliable because he often comes too late.

urealistisk.explanation: "Urealistisk" means "unrealistic". It is built from "u-" (not) and "realistisk" (realistic). To say a goal can work in real life: "Det er et realistisk mål" (It is a realistic goal).

sentence.da: Det er **urealistisk** at lære dansk perfekt på en måned.
sentence.en: It is unrealistic to learn Danish perfectly in a month.

urimelig.explanation: "Urimelig" means "unreasonable", used when something is too much or not fair. The opposite is "rimelig" (reasonable), which you also say about a fair price: "en rimelig pris" (a reasonable price).

sentence.da: Det er en **urimelig** regel, at børn ikke må lege her.
sentence.en: It is an unreasonable rule that children may not play here.

urolig.explanation: "Urolig" means "uneasy". It is built from "u-" (not) and "rolig" (calm). To say you worry about someone, add "for" (about): "Han er urolig for sin hund" (He is uneasy about his dog). It also means "restless". For example, "en urolig nat" (a restless night).

sentence.da: Jeg er **urolig** for min søster.
sentence.en: I am uneasy about my sister.

usa.explanation: "USA" means "the USA". To say where someone lives, use "i" (in): "Jeg bor i USA" (I live in the USA). Danes say the three letters one by one: "u", "es", "a".

sentence.da: New York ligger i **USA**.
sentence.en: New York is in the USA.

uselvisk.explanation: "Uselvisk" means "unselfish". It is built from "u-" (un-) and "selvisk" (selfish).

sentence.da: Hun er **uselvisk** og hjælper altid andre før sig selv.
sentence.en: She is unselfish and always helps others before herself.

usikker.explanation: "Usikker" means "unsure". When you say something is not safe, it means "unsafe": "en usikker bro" (an unsafe bridge).

sentence.da: Jeg er **usikker** på, hvad jeg skal sige.
sentence.en: I am unsure what I should say.

uskadt.explanation: "Uskadt" means "unhurt". When you talk about a thing after a storm or an accident, it means "undamaged": "Huset er uskadt" (The house is undamaged).

sentence.da: Bilen er helt ødelagt, men føreren er **uskadt**.
sentence.en: The car is completely wrecked, but the driver is unhurt.

uskarp.explanation: "Uskarp" means "blurry". It is built from "u-" (not) and "skarp" (sharp).

sentence.da: Min skærm er **uskarp**, så jeg kan ikke læse teksten.
sentence.en: My screen is blurry, so I cannot read the text.

uskyld.explanation: "En uskyld" means "innocence". When you talk about a child's lack of experience of the world, use it for that too: "barnets uskyld" (the child's innocence).

sentence.da: Han kunne bevise sin **uskyld**, og retten løslod ham.
sentence.en: He could prove his innocence, and the court released him.

uskyldig.explanation: "Uskyldig" means "innocent". When you describe a joke that is meant harmlessly, use it too: "Det er en uskyldig joke" (It is an innocent joke).

sentence.da: Dommeren sagde, at han var **uskyldig**.
sentence.en: The judge said that he was innocent.

ustabil.explanation: "Ustabil" means "unstable". It is built from "u-" (not) and "stabil" (stable). To describe an internet connection that keeps failing, say: "Forbindelsen er ustabil" (The connection is unstable).

sentence.da: Stolen er **ustabil**, fordi et ben er kort.
sentence.en: The chair is unstable because one leg is short.

usund.explanation: "Usund" means "unhealthy". It is built from "u-" (not) and "sund" (healthy). To say a habit is bad for you, say: "Rygning er usundt" (Smoking is unhealthy).

sentence.da: Slik og kage er **usund** mad.
sentence.en: Candy and cake are unhealthy food.

usympatisk.explanation: "Usympatisk" means "unlikeable". English speakers may expect it to mean "unsympathetic", but it does not. To say someone feels for others, use "medfølende" (compassionate): "Hun er medfølende" (She is compassionate).

sentence.da: Manden virkede **usympatisk**, fordi han aldrig smilede.
sentence.en: The man seemed unlikeable because he never smiled.

usynlig.explanation: "Usynlig" means "invisible". To say you can see something, use "synlig" (visible): "Stjernen er synlig" (The star is visible).

sentence.da: Luften er **usynlig**, men vi trækker vejret.
sentence.en: The air is invisible, but we breathe.

usædvanlig.explanation: "Usædvanlig" means "unusual". It is built from "u-" (not) and "sædvanlig" (usual).

sentence.da: Det er en **usædvanlig** lyd, og jeg kender den ikke.
sentence.en: It is an unusual sound, and I do not know it.

utaknemmelig.explanation: "Utaknemmelig" means "ungrateful". When you describe a job that brings little reward, it means "thankless": "en utaknemmelig opgave" (a thankless task).

sentence.da: Han var **utaknemmelig** og sagde aldrig tak for hjælpen.
sentence.en: He was ungrateful and never said thanks for the help.

utallige.explanation: "Utallige" means "countless". When you talk about more than one thing, put it before the plural noun: "utallige stjerner" (countless stars).

sentence.da: Der er **utallige** stjerner på himlen en klar nat.
sentence.en: There are countless stars in the sky on a clear night.

utilfreds.explanation: "Utilfreds" means "dissatisfied". It is built from "u-" (not) and "tilfreds" (satisfied). To say what you are dissatisfied with, add "med" (with): "utilfreds med lønnen" (dissatisfied with the pay).

sentence.da: Kunden er **utilfreds** med maden.
sentence.en: The customer is dissatisfied with the food.

utilfredshed.explanation: "En utilfredshed" means "dissatisfaction". It is the noun for the adjective "utilfreds" (dissatisfied). To say what you are dissatisfied with, add "med" (with): "utilfredshed med servicen" (dissatisfaction with the service).

sentence.da: Der er **utilfredshed** blandt kunderne, fordi leveringen er sen.
sentence.en: There is dissatisfaction among the customers because the delivery is late.

utilstrækkelig.explanation: "Utilstrækkelig" means "inadequate". When you describe a person who feels not good enough, it describes that person too: "Jeg føler mig utilstrækkelig" (I feel inadequate).

sentence.da: Hjælpen var **utilstrækkelig**, fordi der kun kom én læge.
sentence.en: The help was inadequate because only one doctor came.

utro.explanation: "Utro" means "unfaithful". It is built from "u-" (not) and "tro" (true). To name the person who is betrayed, add "mod" (toward): "Han har været utro mod hende" (He has been unfaithful to her).

sentence.da: Han var **utro**, og hun blev meget ked af det.
sentence.en: He was unfaithful, and she became very sad.

utrolig.explanation: "Utrolig" means "unbelievable". It is built from "at tro" (to believe) and "u-" (not). To react to surprising news, say: "Det er utroligt!" (That is unbelievable!).

sentence.da: Det er en **utrolig** historie, men den er sand.
sentence.en: It is an unbelievable story, but it is true.

utroligt.explanation: "Utroligt" means "incredibly". It comes from the adjective "utrolig" (unbelievable). To make an adjective stronger, put it before the adjective: "Det er utroligt varmt i dag" (It is incredibly hot today).

sentence.da: Bjerget er **utroligt** højt.
sentence.en: The mountain is incredibly high.

utydelig.explanation: "Utydelig" means "unclear". It is built from "u-" (not) and "tydelig" (clear). To describe handwriting that is hard to read, say: "utydelig skrift" (unclear handwriting).

sentence.da: Hans stemme er **utydelig**, fordi forbindelsen er dårlig.
sentence.en: His voice is unclear because the connection is bad.

utålmodig.explanation: "Utålmodig" means "impatient". It is built from "u-" (not) and "tålmodig" (patient). To tell someone to wait, say: "Vær ikke så utålmodig!" (Do not be so impatient!).

sentence.da: Jeg er **utålmodig**, for bussen er forsinket.
sentence.en: I am impatient, because the bus is late.

utålmodighed.explanation: "En utålmodighed" means "impatience". It is the noun for the adjective "utålmodig" (impatient). To say how someone waited, use "med" (with): "Hun ventede med utålmodighed" (She waited with impatience).

sentence.da: Børnenes **utålmodighed** vokser, fordi bilturen er lang.
sentence.en: The children's impatience grows because the car trip is long.

uundgåelig.explanation: "Uundgåelig" means "unavoidable". To say something will happen anyway, say: "Forsinkelser er uundgåelige" (Delays are unavoidable).

sentence.da: Konflikten var **uundgåelig**, fordi ingen ville give sig.
sentence.en: The conflict was inevitable because no one would give in.

uundværlig.explanation: "Uundværlig" means "indispensable". It comes from "at undvære" (to do without). To say you cannot do without your phone, say: "Min telefon er uundværlig" (My phone is indispensable).

sentence.da: Min kaffe er **uundværlig**, når jeg skal op tidligt.
sentence.en: My coffee is indispensable when I have to get up early.

uvant.explanation: "Uvant" means "unfamiliar". It is built from "u-" (not) and "vant" (used to). To say what you are not used to, add "med" (with): "Jeg er uvant med kulden" (I am not used to the cold).

sentence.da: Jeg er **uvant** med at stå op så tidligt.
sentence.en: I am not used to getting up so early.

uvedkommende.explanation: "Uvedkommende" means "unauthorized". When you say a question has nothing to do with the matter, it means "irrelevant": "et uvedkommende spørgsmål" (an irrelevant question). To keep people out of a place, a sign says: "Adgang forbudt for uvedkommende" (No entry for unauthorized persons).

sentence.da: Det, du siger, er **uvedkommende** for sagen.
sentence.en: What you are saying is irrelevant to the case.

uvenlig.explanation: "Uvenlig" means "unfriendly". It is built from "u-" (not) and "venlig" (friendly). To name the person who receives the unfriendly behavior, add "mod" (toward): "Hun var uvenlig mod mig" (She was unfriendly to me).

sentence.da: Han var **uvenlig** og sagde ikke goddag.
sentence.en: He was unfriendly and did not say hello.

uventet.explanation: "Uventet" means "unexpected". To say something came as a surprise, put it after the verb: "Det kom helt uventet" (It came completely unexpectedly).

sentence.da: Besøget var **uventet**, fordi ingen havde ringet.
sentence.en: The visit was unexpected because no one had called.

uvidende.explanation: "Uvidende" means "unaware". It is built from "u-" (not) and "at vide" (to know). To name the subject you know nothing about, add "om" (about): "Jeg er uvidende om reglerne" (I am unaware of the rules).

forms.en: a child who does not know

sentence.da: Hun var **uvidende** om planen, fordi ingen havde fortalt hende det.
sentence.en: She was unaware of the plan because no one had told her.

uvidenhed.explanation: "En uvidenhed" means "ignorance". It is the noun for the adjective "uvidende" (unaware). To name the subject you know nothing about, add "om" (about): "uvidenhed om reglerne" (ignorance of the rules).

sentence.da: Fejlen skyldtes **uvidenhed**, ikke ond vilje.
sentence.en: The mistake was due to ignorance, not ill will.

uærlig.explanation: "Uærlig" means "dishonest". It is built from "u-" (not) and "ærlig" (honest).

sentence.da: Han er **uærlig** og snyder tit i spil.
sentence.en: He is dishonest and often cheats at games.
